title: Dipyridamole alleviates necroptosis and renal inflammation via cAMP/CREB signaling pathways in septic AKI mice.
authors: Xing, Jia; Lin, Geng; Chen, Zhao-Xuan; Zhao, Wan-Ting; Mo, Shu-Wen; Zhai, Xiao-Yue; Zhang, Jie
one_liner_zh: 该文研究双嘧达莫通过cAMP/CREB信号通路缓解脓毒症相关急性肾损伤，核心为药物-蛋白（PDE12）互作与肾脏病理，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a severe complication characterized by inflammation, hemodynamic instability, and organ dysfunction, with high morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in supportive care, targeted therapies remain limited. Given the critical role of cAMP signaling in immune regulation and cellular homeostasis, this study explored the therapeutic potential of dipyridamole, a phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitor, mitigating SA-AKI. METHODS: Transcriptomic profiling of kidneys from LPS-induced SA-AKI and control mice was performed to identify dysregulated pathways. The effects of dipyridamole on renal pathology and function were evaluated using biochemical assays, PAS staining, TUNEL staining, electron microscopy, and immunohistochemistry. Mechanistic studies included ELISA, qPCR, western blotting, molecular docking, and PDE12 knockdown in TCMK-1 cells with siRNA transfection. RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis revealed widespread dysfunction of inflammatory and metabolic pathways in SA-AKI kidneys, with upregulation of NF-kappaB/TLR signaling and suppression of cAMP-related pathways. Among PDE isoforms, PDE12 was most significantly upregulated, and molecular docking demonstrated strong binding of dipyridamole to PDE12. Dipyridamole treatment restored cAMP levels, enhanced CREB phosphorylation, suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha and IL-6), and attenuated necroptosis via inhibition of RIPK3/MLKL signaling. Importantly, siRNA-mediated PDE12 knockdown reproduced these protective effects, confirming PDE12 as a pathogenic mediator of LPS-induced tubular injury. These molecular and cellular changes translated into significant improvements in renal function and histological integrity. CONCLUSIONS: Dipyridamole alleviates SA-AKI by targeting PDE12, restoring cAMP signaling, and suppressing inflammation and necroptosis. These findings highlight PDE12 as a novel therapeutic target and support dipyridamole as a promising candidate for clinical translation in SA-AKI.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症相关急性肾损伤（SA-AKI）是一种严重并发症，以炎症、血流动力学不稳定和器官功能障碍为特征，具有高发病率和死亡率。尽管支持性治疗有所进展，但靶向治疗仍有限。鉴于cAMP信号在免疫调节和细胞稳态中的关键作用，本研究探讨了双嘧达莫（一种磷酸二酯酶（PDE）抑制剂）缓解SA-AKI的治疗潜力。方法：对LPS诱导的SA-AKI和对照小鼠肾脏进行转录组学分析，以识别失调通路。通过生化检测、PAS染色、TUNEL染色、电子显微镜和免疫组化评估双嘧达莫对肾脏病理和功能的影响。机制研究包括ELISA、qPCR、western blotting、分子对接以及通过siRNA转染在TCMK-1细胞中进行PDE12敲低。结果：转录组学分析揭示SA-AKI肾脏中炎症和代谢通路广泛功能障碍，NF-kappaB/TLR信号上调，cAMP相关通路受抑制。在PDE亚型中，PDE12上调最为显著，分子对接显示双嘧达莫与PDE12具有强结合力。双嘧达莫治疗恢复cAMP水平，增强CREB磷酸化，抑制促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha和IL-6），并通过抑制RIPK3/MLKL信号减轻坏死性凋亡。重要的是，siRNA介导的PDE12敲低重现了这些保护效应，确认PDE12是LPS诱导的肾小管损伤的致病介质。这些分子和细胞变化转化为肾功能和组织学完整性的显著改善。结论：双嘧达莫通过靶向PDE12、恢复cAMP信号以及抑制炎症和坏死性凋亡来缓解SA-AKI。这些发现突出PDE12作为新型治疗靶点，并支持双嘧达莫作为SA-AKI临床转化的有前景候选药物。
